extra_misconceptions.fact: Columns and pediments appear across Neoclassical, Federal, and Colonial Revival styles, so you must check window and roof proportions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every building featuring white front columns and a triangular pediment belongs to the ancient Greek Revival period.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective field sketches focus on overall massing, roof pitch, fenestration patterns, and key structural proportions rather than texture.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An architectural field sketch requires photorealistic shading of every brick and shingle to be useful for style analysis.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ancient Roman concrete lacked steel reinforcement and relied on volcanic ash mortar with thick arches to handle compressive loads.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Roman concrete and modern reinforced concrete share the exact same tensile strength and internal steel rebar grid.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Architectural style is defined by permanent structural elements, roof form, window geometry, and period construction materials.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A building's current commercial tenant or interior paint scheme determines its formal architectural style classification.

extra_socratic_questions: Which structural detail distinguishes a load-bearing masonry arch from a decorative veneer arch on a community building?
Where should a Scout stand on a busy sidewalk to sketch a building facade without blocking pedestrian traffic or driveways?
What proportion benchmark helps you keep window spacing and roofline angles accurate when sketching a building in the field?
In what way did the invention of structural steel frames change maximum building height compared to thick stone walls?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Renewable materials grow back quickly from living sources like cork or bamboo, while recycled materials reprocess post-consumer waste.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Recycled building materials and renewable building materials mean the exact same thing in green construction specifications.

extra_misconceptions.fact: True sustainable architecture reduces heating and cooling demand first through tight envelope insulation, passive solar, and shading.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding rooftop solar panels to a poorly insulated building automatically makes the structure energy-efficient and sustainable.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Adaptive reuse preserves the massive embodied energy already spent manufacturing and transporting the original brick, steel, and concrete.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Demolishing an older masonry building always uses less energy over time than renovating it for a new community purpose.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vegetated roof systems absorb rainwater to reduce sewer overflow, insulate the roof deck, and lower urban heat island temperatures.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Green roofs are installed solely for visual appeal and add no measurable thermal or stormwater benefit to an urban building.

extra_socratic_questions: What physical property separates a rapidly renewable material like bamboo from a recycled material like crushed steel slag?
Under what climate condition does orienting large glass windows toward the south reduce winter heating loads in a building?
What happens to neighborhood stormwater runoff when a new development replaces permeable soil with dark asphalt parking lots?
Why is adaptive reuse of an existing brick warehouse often greener than demolishing it to build a new efficient structure?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scale models show three-dimensional massing and light, while construction drawings specify fasteners, flashing, and structural connections.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A physical presentation model shows contractors the exact bolt sizes, flashing layers, and wall insulation needed to build.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Material selection balances structural capacity, fire rating, moisture resistance, thermal expansion, maintenance cost, and local climate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Architects pick exterior building materials based only on color and visual texture without considering local weather loads.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Complete construction sets pair floor plans with exterior elevations, building sections, and enlarged connection details for every assembly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Construction blueprints consist only of top-down floor plans and leave wall heights and roof slopes up to the carpenter.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Architectural programming documents occupant headcounts, workflow adjacency, ADA accessibility, mechanical needs, and strict budget limits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Client interviews only cover exterior style preferences rather than daily room traffic, budget limits, or accessibility needs.

extra_socratic_questions: What information appears on a cross-section detail drawing that cannot be seen on the exterior of a physical scale model?
Which protective gear must you wear before walking onto an active construction site with an architect or project manager?
What happens to a structural connection if incompatible metals like bare steel and copper touch in a wet exterior wall?
Which client functional requirements must an architect record during programming before sketching a single floor plan?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Twelve feet multiplied by one-quarter inch per foot equals exactly 3 inches on the scaled floor plan drawing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: At a drawing scale of 1/4 inch equals 1 foot, a 12-foot bedroom wall should be drawn 4 inches long on your paper.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Short segment measurements accumulate rounding errors at every mark, so always record a continuous overall wall dimension to verify totals.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Measuring along one wall in short segments and adding them up is more accurate than pulling one continuous tape measurement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard floor plans draw wall thickness with double lines, curved arcs for door swing clearance, and glass lines for window openings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Doors and windows can be drawn as simple gaps in a single line without showing swing arcs or sill locations on a floor plan.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Permanent cabinets, closets, and hearth projections define fixed circulation paths and must be measured and plotted to scale.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Built-in cabinets and closets can be left off a room floor plan because they do not affect usable furniture floor area.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement on your graph paper represents a 10-foot wall when you draw a floor plan at a 1/4 inch = 1 foot scale?
Why is it important to measure overall wall-to-wall diagonals in addition to individual wall segments in an older room?
Which architectural symbol on a floor plan shows the direction a hinged door swings and the floor space it requires?
Where should you anchor the zero end of a steel tape measure to avoid scratching painted baseboards or pinching fingers?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Graduates must complete the Architectural Experience Program hours and pass all divisions of the Architect Registration Examination first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating from college with a bachelor's degree in architecture immediately grants legal authority to call yourself an architect.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Landscape architects design grading, stormwater drainage, public parks, pedestrian plazas, and ecological site restoration systems.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Landscape architects only select decorative garden flowers and lawn shrubs for residential backyards after construction ends.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern architects spend much of their week coordinating structural, mechanical, and electrical engineers alongside builders and clients.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Licensed architects work alone at drafting boards all day and rarely coordinate with engineers, code officials, or contractors.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Professional NAAB-accredited Bachelor of Architecture programs typically require five years of intensive studio and technical coursework.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any NAAB-accredited architecture degree takes the exact same number of years as a standard non-accredited art degree.

extra_socratic_questions: What is the legal difference between earning a university architecture degree and becoming a licensed registered architect?
Which public safety responsibilities require a licensed architect to stamp and seal official building construction drawings?
What distinct project problems does a landscape architect solve compared to a structural engineer or urban planner?
Why must an architectural intern log thousands of supervised practice hours across multiple project phases before licensing?
